question: ________ is the branch of science that aims at improving the genetic quality of human population.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Eugenics**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eugenics** is the branch of science that aims at improving the genetic quality of the human population.
 
• The term **eugenics** was coined by Francis Galton in the late 19th century.
 
• It involves selective breeding, genetic screening, and other biotechnological interventions to promote desired genetic traits.
 
• While eugenics has historical significance, it is a controversial field due to its association with unethical practices in the past, including forced sterilizations and discriminatory policies.
 
• Modern discussions on eugenics often focus on ethical considerations and the potential for genetic technologies to be used responsibly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biotechnology** is a broader field that includes the use of living systems and organisms to develop products.
 
• **Genetics** is the study of genes, genetic variation, and heredity in organisms.
 
• **Epigenetics** is the study of heritable changes in gene expression that do not involve changes to the underlying DNA sequence.
